decisions.reason: As a two-component resin injection unit, it sits squarely in the firm's core application-technology business, and prior engineering and marketing commitment make management likely to continue unless failure is unmistakable.
This product is also central to the firm's established injection-equipment portfolio, so sunk development effort and the tendency to justify the launch support keeping it on the market.

An automatic airless spray gun fits the firm's announced push in innovative application technology, making management inclined to persist and attribute any weak uptake to market timing rather than abandon it quickly.
A manual airless spray gun is closely tied to the firm's core spray-equipment range, so it is easy to defend as a necessary portfolio offering and likely to be retained.
The air-assisted airless spray gun remains highly consistent with the firm's technical capabilities and customer base, which encourages continued support despite any disappointing early results.

Although the data logger matches the innovation narrative, its weaker website prominence after launch suggests softer commitment and makes it the easiest product for management to discontinue if resources are tightened.
